the dependence between international equity returns and between international bond returns is high in both the normal and the asymmetric regime, while the dependence of equity returns with bond returns is low in the same country and low between countries in the normal regime.

equity returns in the US and Canada and in France and Germany are more dependent during bear markets than during bull markets, and that this phenomenon is due to extreme dependence that is not present in a multivariate normal model.
the dependence of international equity and bond returns is large and that this dependence is asymmetric in the sense that the dependence is larger in bear markets than it is in bull markets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extreme comovements in international equity and bond returns.
the dependence structure of international equity and bond returns.
the dependence structure between international equity and bond returns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dependence between international equities and bonds, and between equities in different countries is asymmetric.
international equity and bond dependence is asymmetric and extreme, and that exchange rate volatility contributes to the asymmetry of dependence.
the dependence between equity and bond markets is low and the dependence between equity markets of two countries is high, especially in the asymmetric regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
extreme dependence is not a normal feature of financial time series, and it is important for the study of financial markets to take into account the asymmetric dependence structure.
the dependence structure of international equity markets is asymmetric and that this asymmetric dependence is due to the presence of extreme comovements.
the tail dependence is a key factor in explaining the asymmetric dependence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dependence between international asset markets is not symmetric and that the asymmetric dependence is not captured by standard models such as a multivariate Garch model or a RS model based on normal innovation.
asymmetric dependence is not an artifact of a misspecified model, but a genuine feature of international equity and bond returns.
extreme dependence in international markets cannot be captured by a standard GARCH or regime switching (RS), model with normal innovations.
